rounds.title: Statistics Interview
rounds.description: Interpret uncertainty, experiments and causality without hiding behind formulas.

questions.context: An A/B test estimates +3% lift, with a 95% interval from -2% to +8%.
options: The estimate is promising but uncertain; the interval includes harm and benefit, so avoid claiming a proven lift
The variant definitely improves conversion by exactly 3%
The test proves there is no effect
Ignore the interval because the point estimate is positive
questions.expectedAnswer: The estimate is promising but uncertain; the interval includes harm and benefit, so avoid claiming a proven lift
questions.explanation: The point estimate and interval should be interpreted together.

questions.context: Users who enable notifications retain better than users who do not.
questions.prompt: Which next step best addresses causality?
options: Randomize an eligible notification intervention or use a credible causal design before making a causal claim
Announce that notifications are the sole reason for retention
Use a pie chart to settle the question
questions.expectedAnswer: Randomize an eligible notification intervention or use a credible causal design before making a causal claim
questions.explanation: Observed adoption can be confounded by user intent or engagement.
